newsitem.title: USA: US spot gas prices hover more than $1 under index.
newsitem.headline: US spot gas prices hover more than $1 under index.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for early January were notionally talked lower Tuesday, pressured by mild forecasts across the U.S. and a weaker industrial load expected this week because of the holiday, traders said.
Swing Gulf Coast prices were notionally about 25 cents lower in the $2.60s early and the $2.40s late, down about $1.50 from most January indices.
Trading was sparse though as most had already locked up their deals through the first few days of the month.
In south Texas, where temperatures as much as 25 degrees above-normal were expected later this week, prices fell into the $2.40s, down 20-25 cents from Monday.
At the New York city-gate, prices rose into the $3.60-3.80 range today despite expectations for above-normal temperatures over at least the next week.
Temperatures in the Mid-Atlantic states are expected to hover near-normal Tuesday and Wednesday but then climb to about eight to 12 degrees Fahrenheit above normal by Saturday.
Some sources noted that the comparable New York fuel oil market should keep gas prices competitive in the near-term.
Midcontinent prices were talked higher in the $2.80s and $2.90s, as compared with Monday's trading range of $2.70-2.75.
At the Chicago city-gate, prices were quoted in the $3.15-3.20 range.
Temperatures throughout most of the Midwest are forecast to remain at least 10 degrees above-normal through this weekend, with temperatures as much as 25 degrees above-normal possible.
In west Texas, where temperatures are about 10-25 degrees above-normal, Permian gas prices fell into the $2.40s, down more than 20 cents from Monday.
In the San Juan basin, prices were talked in the $2.30s.
